_comment: Arizona 2026 and 2027 QAP, Arizona Department of Housing. The cover reads 'Submitted on December 1, 2025 and amended on ____ by:', with the amendment date left blank, although the introduction says ADOH 'has adopted this QAP for 2026 and amended it for 2027'; which version this is should be confirmed at the source. Page numbers are PDF page indices and match the printed page numbers (the table of contents does not: it lists II.G on page 7 after II.F on page 10). Selection Criteria are Section V, pp.16-25. 4% LIHTC applications are not scored (V.A). THREE SCORING UNIVERSES, recorded as tracks. 'rehab' is V.B, 9% LIHTC Rehabilitation, five criteria totalling 170. The default track is V.C, 9% LIHTC New Construction (Rural and Metro) and Tribal, eight criteria totalling 185. 'tribal' is the one criterion V.C.9 LOCCS Balance, 25 points, which applies only in the Tribal set-aside on top of the default track, so a Tribal new construction project faces 210. No track states a total. Every criterion states its own maximum, and each was hand-summed before loading (rehab 35 + 60 + 40 + 10 + 25; new construction 25 + 30 + 40 + 10 + 25 + 20 + 15 + 20). The only stated figure is a floor: 'a minimum total score of one hundred sixty (160) points', in IV.C.6 under the New Construction threshold heading, whose text refers to 'the competitive 9% LIHTC round'. Whether it binds rehab applications, for which it would be 94% of the maximum, is unclear. Thresholds are in AZ_thresholds.json.

track_totals.note: No total stated. 9% New Construction (Rural and Metro, and Tribal before its add-on): the eight criteria's stated maxima sum to 185, which the loader matches. The 160-point minimum in IV.C.6 (p.16) is 86% of 185. Two criteria (V.C.2 and V.C.5) list items worth more than their stated maxima and are capped at them.

No total stated. 9% Rehabilitation set-aside (up to two awards): the five criteria's stated maxima sum to 170. If the 160-point minimum in IV.C.6 applies here too, a rehab project could miss only 10 points.

Add-on for the Tribal set-aside: V.C.9 LOCCS Balance, 25 points, on top of the default track's 185, for 210 in all. Tribal projects outside Tribal land compete in Rural or Metro instead and cannot earn this.

criteria.heading: Project type
criteria.quote: ADOH will award up to thirty-five (35) points based on the following:

tiers.tier_label: Existing USDA or other federally funded project
Existing LIHTC project, or federally funded project with project-based rent subsidy covering at least 70% of units

criteria.note: Rewards preserving existing subsidized stock over reoccupying vacant buildings.

criteria.heading: Rehabilitation work (hard cost per unit)
criteria.quote: Maximum of sixty (60) points.
criteria.note: The largest criterion in the rehab track, and it pays for spending more per unit, supported by a third-party CNA and a scope meeting Exhibit A. The threshold minimum is $25,000 per unit (IV.B.2), so $25,000-$30,000 is eligible but scores 0; exactly $30,000 falls between the first two rows.

criteria.heading: Project-based rental assistance
criteria.quote: ADOH will award up to forty (40) points for the percentage of total units supported by project-based rent
criteria.note: The bottom row pays 10 points for '15% or less', which as written includes a project with any assistance at all; the text does not say whether 0% scores. Project-based rent assistance or federally funded operating subsidy both count.

criteria.heading: Community revitalization plans, QCTs, DDAs and opportunity zones
criteria.quote: ADOH will award five (5) points to applications that are located within a:

tiers.tier_label: Qualified Census Tract (at least one building)

criteria.note: Five points per designation, capped at 10, so any two suffice. The CRP must be adopted by a local government before the deadline, name a revitalization area containing the site, carry non-housing investment commitments, and not have been initiated by a Principal. A QCT needs only one building inside it; a DDA or OZ needs all of them.

criteria.heading: Developer's experience
criteria.quote: 5. DEVELOPER’S EXPERIENCE
criteria.note: Distinct LIHTC or federally subsidized projects placed in service by the developer, co-developer or a consultant. A consultant supplying the experience must stay involved through 8609 and cannot be dropped without ADOH approval. Identical to V.C.1.

criteria.heading: Greatest total number of LIHTC units
criteria.quote: contains the greatest total number of LIHTC units;

criteria.heading: Lowest AMI average of the rent-restricted units
criteria.quote: has the lowest AMI average of the rent restricted units

criteria.heading: Longest extended use period
criteria.quote: has the longest extended use period.

criteria.heading: Developer's experience
criteria.quote: 1. DEVELOPER’S EXPERIENCE
criteria.note: Identical to V.B.5 in the rehab track. ADOH scores only 'the highest-ranking self-scored applications in their respective set-asides', so the self-score decides which applications are reviewed at all.

criteria.heading: Supportive housing
criteria.quote: Tenant Based Rental Assistance Participation

tiers.tier_label: Commit to lease at least 15% of units to households with tenant-based rental assistance
Project-based rental assistance targeted to special populations, 15% of units
Project-based rental assistance targeted to special populations, 30% of units or more

criteria.note: Two routes under a 30-point maximum. The text does not say whether they combine, but the tenant-based route alone reaches the cap, which makes the question moot for scoring. The tenant-based route asks only for a commitment to lease to voucher holders; the project-based route needs third-party vouchers for units at 30% AMI, an ADOH-approved targeting plan with units held open 60 days after certificate of occupancy, and a supportive services plan. The same 30 points are available either way.

criteria.heading: Proximity to amenities
criteria.quote: PROXIMITY TO AMENITIES

tiers.tier_label: Grocery (named chains, or others by request)
Bus or transit stop (6 days a week in Valley Metro/Sun Tran areas, 5 elsewhere)
Employment center (250 FTE metro, 50 rural, 30 tribal)
Other amenities, 2 points each from twelve types, maximum 10

criteria.note: The six items sum to the stated 40. Driving distance by Google Maps: 2.5 miles metro, 4 miles rural, 15 miles on Tribal land. The same establishment may count under several categories, so one Walmart Supercenter can supply grocery and shopping. The grocery list names specific chains.

criteria.heading: Community revitalization plans, QCTs, DDAs and opportunity zones
criteria.quote: ADOH will award points based on the criteria described in QAP Section V(B)(4).
criteria.note: Incorporates V.B.4 by reference: 5 points per designation, capped at 10. The tier values are read from p.17, where V.B.4 states them.

criteria.heading: Below market loans and local support
criteria.quote: BELOW MARKET LOANS AND LOCAL SUPPORT

tiers.tier_label: Local gap financing loans ($500,000 metro, $100,000 rural and tribal)
Eligible for the federal historic rehabilitation tax credit
Land lease from local government or non-affiliated 501(c)(3), at most $2,000 a month
Local fee waivers ($100,000 metro, $50,000 rural and tribal)

criteria.note: Five items totalling 30 against a stated maximum of 25. Sources affiliated with a Principal may be disregarded, and a local government's loan is reduced by the price of any land it sells to the project. A historic-credit item inside the new construction track presumably serves adaptive reuse, which the New Construction set-aside includes.

criteria.heading: Senior and family
criteria.quote: Applications will earn twenty (20) points for agreeing to comply with one of the following two options.

tiers.tier_label: Senior housing with at least three of eight listed services or features
Family property with at least 20% of units of three or more bedrooms

criteria.note: Either option pays the full 20, so almost every project can claim it; it sorts projects into senior and family rather than ranking them.

criteria.heading: Energy efficiency and heat mitigation
criteria.quote: ENERGY EFFICIENCY & HEAT MITIGATION

tiers.tier_label: Certification: Enterprise Green Communities, LEED Silver, NGBS Silver, or DOE Zero Energy Ready

criteria.note: 10 + 5 = the stated 15. Despite the heading, nothing in the section addresses heat mitigation specifically; both items are energy certifications or ratings.

criteria.heading: Increase in extended use period or homeownership
criteria.quote: INCREASE IN EXTENDED USE PERIOD OR HOMEOWNERSHIP
criteria.note: Joined by 'or'. Five points per additional five years beyond the 30-year minimum, to 50 years. Homeownership conversion pays only 10 and is limited to single-family or townhome projects on Tribal land or qualifying for a nonprofit adjustment.

criteria.heading: LOCCS balance (Tribal set-aside only)
criteria.quote: LOCCS BALANCE (Tribal Set Aside Only)

tiers.tier_label: Unexpended NAHASDA funds less than the greater of $1 million or one full year
One full year but less than two, 'or the greater of $2 million'

criteria.note: Rewards tribes that have spent their NAHASDA funds: the smaller the unexpended LOCCS balance, the higher the score, and a balance of two years or more earns nothing. The second tier's wording ('One (1) full year but less than two (2) full years or the greater of $2 million') does not parse cleanly and should be read by a reviewer on p.25.
